BUS.G11.T2.ACTIONPLAN.A1.title: From business plan to action plan
BUS.G11.T2.ACTIONPLAN.A1.description: Transforming a business plan into an action plan using planning tools — Gantt charts and a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) with timelines and responsibilities — so that the plan becomes a sequence of dated, assigned tasks.
BUS.G11.T2.ACTIONPLAN.A1.strand: T2 — Creative thinking, stress & change, action plans, setting up, ethics & presentation
BUS.G11.T2.ACTIONPLAN.A1.recovery_strategy: A business plan says WHAT and WHY; an action plan says WHO does WHICH task by WHEN. A Gantt chart shows tasks against a timeline; a WBS breaks the work into smaller tasks.

questions.question: What does an action plan mainly show?
options: Who does which task, and by when
Only the company's profit for last year
questions.expected: Who does which task, and by when
questions.memo: An action plan turns goals into concrete tasks, each with a person responsible and a deadline.

questions.question: A _________ chart shows tasks plotted against a timeline.
questions.expected: Gantt
questions.memo: A Gantt chart lists tasks down the side and time along the top, showing when each task starts, ends and overlaps.

questions.question: True or false: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) splits a big project into smaller tasks.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: A WBS breaks a large project into smaller, manageable tasks so the work can be planned and assigned.

questions.question: What is the difference between a business plan and an action plan?
options: A business plan says what and why; an action plan says who does what by when
A business plan is illegal; an action plan is legal
They are exactly the same document
An action plan is only about marketing
questions.expected: A business plan says what and why; an action plan says who does what by when
questions.memo: The business plan sets out the idea and the reasons; the action plan turns it into dated, assigned tasks.

questions.question: In the planning tool 'WBS', the letters stand for Work _________ Structure.
questions.expected: Breakdown
questions.memo: WBS stands for Work Breakdown Structure — a tool that breaks a project down into smaller tasks.

questions.question: True or false: An action plan assigns responsibilities to specific people.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: An action plan names who is responsible for each task, so everyone knows what they must do.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it belongs in the business plan or the action plan.

items.text: A Gantt chart of tasks and dates
A list of who is responsible for each task

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Big-picture items (summary, vision, SWOT) belong in the business plan; dated, assigned tasks (Gantt, responsibilities, timeline) belong in the action plan.

questions.question: What does a Gantt chart help a manager to see at a glance?
options: Which tasks happen when, and which overlap
How much profit was made last year
The history of the company logo
questions.expected: Which tasks happen when, and which overlap
questions.memo: A Gantt chart shows the timing of tasks, including which run in parallel, helping a manager track progress.

questions.question: Put the steps of turning a business plan into an action plan in order.

items.text: Break the goals into smaller tasks (WBS)
Schedule the tasks on a timeline (Gantt chart)
Assign each task to a responsible person

questions.expected: plan, wbs, schedule, assign
questions.memo: Start from the plan's goals, break them into tasks, schedule those tasks, and assign each one to someone.

questions.question: Each task on an action plan should have a deadline and a person _________ for it.
questions.expected: responsible
questions.memo: Naming a responsible person for each task creates accountability, so tasks actually get done.

questions.question: Why does an action plan include timelines?
options: To keep the project on schedule and track progress
To hide the deadlines from staff
questions.expected: To keep the project on schedule and track progress
questions.memo: Timelines set deadlines so the team can stay on track and see whether the project is progressing as planned.

questions.question: True or false: A Gantt chart can show two or more tasks running at the same time.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Because a Gantt chart plots tasks against time, overlapping bars show tasks that run in parallel.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is a planning tool or not.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Gantt charts, a WBS, timelines and responsibility lists help plan and manage tasks; a mug or a parking sign do not.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of a Work Breakdown Structure?
options: It makes a big project manageable by splitting it into smaller tasks
It hides the size of the project
It removes the need for any deadlines
It guarantees the project costs nothing
questions.expected: It makes a big project manageable by splitting it into smaller tasks
questions.memo: Breaking a project into smaller tasks makes it easier to plan, schedule, assign and track.

questions.question: Why is an action plan so useful once a business plan is written?
options: It turns intentions into concrete, dated steps people can act on
It replaces the need to do any work
It keeps the goals secret from the team
It only repeats the executive summary
questions.expected: It turns intentions into concrete, dated steps people can act on
questions.memo: An action plan converts the broad intentions of the business plan into specific tasks, deadlines and responsibilities.

questions.question: A _________ shows the start and end dates of each task in a project.
questions.expected: timeline
questions.memo: A timeline lays out when each task starts and finishes, helping the team see the schedule.

questions.question: Put the actions in order when launching a new product from a business plan.

items.text: Set the goal: launch the new product
List all the tasks needed (design, produce, market)
Give each task a deadline on a Gantt chart
Assign each task to a team member

questions.expected: goal, tasks, dates, owners
questions.memo: Define the goal, break it into tasks, schedule them with deadlines, then assign each to someone — that is the plan-to-action sequence.

questions.question: An action plan lists tasks but gives no deadlines and names no one responsible. Why is this likely to fail?
options: With no deadlines or owners, no one is accountable and tasks slip
Because action plans should never list tasks
Because deadlines always slow a project down
questions.expected: With no deadlines or owners, no one is accountable and tasks slip
questions.memo: An action plan only works if each task has a deadline and a responsible person; without these, accountability disappears and work stalls.

questions.question: Why might a project manager use both a WBS and a Gantt chart together?
options: The WBS lists all the tasks; the Gantt chart schedules them over time
They are identical, so using both is a mistake
The WBS hides tasks the Gantt chart shows
questions.expected: The WBS lists all the tasks; the Gantt chart schedules them over time
questions.memo: A WBS first identifies every task; a Gantt chart then places those tasks on a timeline — the two tools complement each other.

questions.question: Two team members both think the other is doing a key task, so it never gets done. Which action-plan feature would have prevented this?
options: Clearly assigning each task to one responsible person
Removing all deadlines from the plan
Hiding the task list from the team
questions.expected: Clearly assigning each task to one responsible person
questions.memo: Assigning each task to a named owner prevents confusion about who is responsible, so nothing falls through the cracks.
